title: A cavity opens in the mesoderm

objective.text: Explain how the embryo's first body cavity forms in weeks 3–4.

body.general: Where do the body's inner spaces come from? At the end of week 3 the middle layer, the mesoderm, forms three strips on each side [f1]. The outer strip, the lateral plate, makes the body cavity [f1]. Small clefts appear in this solid strip and merge, splitting it into two sheets [f2]. The gap between the sheets is the first body cavity, or coelom [f2]. So it opens inside the middle layer, not between the outer layer (ectoderm) and the inner layer (endoderm) [f2]. At first it is one single space, not yet divided [f3].
body.mbbs: By the end of week 3 intraembryonic mesoderm has formed paraxial, intermediate and lateral plate strips [f1]. The lateral plate builds the body cavity [f1]. Clefts appear in the solid lateral plate and merge, splitting it into parietal and visceral layers [f2]. The space between them is the primitive (intraembryonic) body cavity [f2]. At first it is one continuous cavity, not yet divided into pericardial, pleural and abdominopelvic parts [f3]. Early on it opens widely into the extraembryonic cavity; the book shows this at about 21 days [f4]. So the coelom forms inside the mesoderm, not between ectoderm and endoderm [f2].

facts.text: At the end of week 3 the intraembryonic mesoderm forms three strips on each side: paraxial, intermediate and, outermost, the lateral plate. The lateral plate is the strip that builds the body cavity.
Clefts in the solid lateral plate merge, splitting it into parietal and visceral layers; the gap between them is the primitive body cavity.
facts.note: R06: vesicles fuse; one CS9 embryo still has separate left and right cavities

facts.text: At first the body cavity is one continuous space, not yet divided into pericardial, pleural and abdominopelvic parts.
Early on the body cavity opens widely into the extraembryonic cavity (book figure: about 21 days).
facts.note: R06 CS9–10: passage seen in advanced CS10 (22–23 d), about 1–2 days later than the book figure, inside the age error (D-030)

facts.text: Beyond Langman: the first part of the cavity to appear is the heart region, a horseshoe of cavity across the head half of the disc.
facts.note: the book shows the pericardial cavity from 22 d

misconceptions.wrong: The body cavity (coelom) forms between the outer layer (ectoderm) and the inner layer (endoderm).
misconceptions.right: It forms inside the middle layer, the lateral plate mesoderm, splitting it into two layers.

checks.prompt: Where does the body cavity first open up?
options: Between the ectoderm and the endoderm
checks.why: The cavity opens within the lateral plate mesoderm, the middle layer, not between the ectoderm and the endoderm.

options: The mesoderm forms three strips on each side
Clefts appear in the lateral plate
The lateral plate splits into two layers with a gap between
checks.why: The lateral plate must exist before it can cleave; merging clefts then split it into two layers.

checks.prompt: What is the body cavity like when it has just formed?
options: Three separate spaces for heart, lungs and belly
checks.why: It starts as one continuous cavity; the walls that divide it come later.

adult: This one cavity is later divided into the heart, lung and belly cavities [f3].

remember.q: Which mesoderm strip makes the body cavity?
How does the body cavity form?
remember.a: Clefts in the lateral plate merge, splitting it into two layers with the cavity between [f2].

remember.q: Is the early body cavity one space or several?
remember.a: One continuous space, not yet divided into heart, lung and belly parts [f3].
